title: A plain typed override ask lifts a refusal, as the plain Opus ask does
why: Owner ask, 12:44 CST Nov 7 (page ask ask-mw6r5ldefg): in other sessions only the bare `override` or `override 15m` works, though he thought overriding was made more dynamic. Only the Opus refusal got a plain-word route (step opus-plain-ask, #1204, #1208). The general override is still keyword-only: decision owner-override says `override 15m please` grants nothing, so an intended `off` never becomes a grant.
note: Owner asked 13:13 CST Nov 7 whether this fell off the map; triage asked the coordinator to start its lane now. Shape: extend the one home, hooks/override.py and the plain-ask judge in call_judge.py, so a plain owner ask such as `go ahead and override that for 15 min` grants the same one-act or timed override. Keep the fail-closed guards of the Opus route: owner-typed prompt only, pasted and notice blocks cut, questions, hedges and negations grant nothing, judge error grants nothing. The 10-minute expiry of an unused one-act override stays. Departs from: decision owner-override (keyword forms only for `override`) — adds a judged plain-word route. Rewrites that record in place; the owner sees the rewrite in the PR. Done: a red test for `override that for 15 minutes please` granting 15 min, and for `don't override` and `should I override?` granting nothing, then green.
